summary.title: Translational accuracy of a tethered ribosome
summary.executive_summary: This study investigates the translational properties of Ribo-T, a tethered ribosome where the small and large subunits are covalently linked via a hybrid rRNA. While previous work established that Ribo-T supports cell growth, albeit with slower doubling times and reduced protein synthesis rates, this paper specifically probes its fidelity in recoding events. Using a dual-reporter system in E. coli, the authors examined -1 and +1 frameshifting, stop codon readthrough, and translation initiation. The results reveal that while Ribo-T maintains wild-type levels of -1 frameshifting, it is severely impaired in +1 frameshifting. Furthermore, Ribo-T exhibits inefficient use of Shine-Dalgarno (SD) sequences for both initiation and frameshiting stimulation. Finally, the study demonstrates that Ribo-T terminates translation less efficiently than wild-type ribosomes, leading to increased stop codon readthrough. These findings suggest that the covalent tethering alters the ribosome's conformational dynamics, specifically affecting its ability to interact with SD sequences and release factors, despite retaining sufficient functionality for viability.

judge_context:
Executive Summary
This study investigates the translational properties of Ribo-T, a tethered ribosome where the small and large subunits are covalently linked via a hybrid rRNA. While previous work established that Ribo-T supports cell growth, albeit with slower doubling times and reduced protein synthesis rates, this paper specifically probes its fidelity in recoding events. Using a dual-reporter system in E. coli, the authors examined -1 and +1 frameshifting, stop codon readthrough, and translation initiation. The results reveal that while Ribo-T maintains wild-type levels of -1 frameshifting, it is severely impaired in +1 frameshifting. Furthermore, Ribo-T exhibits inefficient use of Shine-Dalgarno (SD) sequences for both initiation and frameshiting stimulation. Finally, the study demonstrates that Ribo-T terminates translation less efficiently than wild-type ribosomes, leading to increased stop codon readthrough. These findings suggest that the covalent tethering alters the ribosome's conformational dynamics, specifically affecting its ability to interact with SD sequences and release factors, despite retaining sufficient functionality for viability.

Research Context
Ribosomes consist of two subunits that associate transiently. The 30S subunit recognizes the Shine-Dalgarno sequence. Tethered ribosomes with covalently linked subunits were engineered. Previous studies showed Ribo-T sustains growth but slower. Recoding events like frameshifting test translation accuracy. It remains unclear why ribosomes have loosely associated subunits. The mutual mobility of subunits is thought to be essential.

Research Question And Hypothesis
Do tethered ribosomes maintain correct reading frames? Do they terminate translation accurately at stop codons? Can Ribo-T use SD sequences for initiation and frameshifting? We hypothesized that covalent attachment modifies ribosome properties. We predicted impairment in initiation and termination accuracy. We investigated behavior in frameshifting and readthrough.

Methodological Details
Experiments used E. coli BL21 (DE3) strain. The poRibo-T2 vector expressed Ribo-T ribosomes. The ASD sequence was altered to an orthogonal sequence. A pCL99 dual reporter system was utilized. The system carries lacZ-luc fusion genes. Target sequences were inserted at the MscI restriction site. Translational efficiency was calculated as a ratio. Significance was determined using Student's t-tests. Wild-type SD was AGGAGG for efficiency analysis. Ribo-T SD was CACCAC for orthogonal initiation.

Procedures And Architectures
Ribo-T has a hybrid rRNA linking small and large subunits. Frameshifting requires a slippery sequence and stimulatory elements. A stem-loop or pseudoknot acts as a stimulatory element. The luciferase reporter measures readthrough and frameshifting. In-frame controls were constructed for each target. The dual reporter monitors translation efficiency. A stable stem loop was inserted to block scanning.

Key Results
-1 frameshifting efficiency was similar for WT and Ribo-T. Ribo-T frameshifted independently of the SD sequence. +1 frameshifting efficiency dropped to 2% for Ribo-T. Ribo-T is unable to sense SD sequences for frameshifting. Ribo-T used SD sequences much less efficiently for initiation. Luciferase induction increased four-fold with Ribo-T SD. Initiation occurred via internal loading, not re-initiation. Readthrough rates were 0.07% vs 0.013% for UAG. Readthrough rates were 0.26% vs 0.11% for UGA. Readthrough rates were 0.04% vs 0.01% for UAA.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
Covalent tethering alters ribosome conformational dynamics. The ASD orientation is likely modified in Ribo-T. This prevents normal SD sequence usage during initiation. Termination efficiency depends on conformational dynamics. The A-site may be less able to bind termination factors. Results highlight the flexibility of ribosomes. Tethering allows sufficient translation for cell viability.

Contradictions And Limitations
Ribo-T growth is slower than wild-type. Protein synthesis rate is 50% of wild-type. Slow growth is attributed to biogenesis, not activity. No natural stop codon readthrough sequence exists in E. coli. High-resolution structure of Ribo-T is not yet available. Mechanism of initiation without SD remains unclear.

Claims
Ribo-T ribosomes maintain -1 frameshifting efficiency independent of SD sequences. Efficiency was 13% for IS911 with both ribosome types. Changing SD had no significant impact on Ribo-T. Ribo-T frameshifts independently of the SD sequence. Ribo-T is impaired in +1 frameshifting. SD-ASD interaction roles differ between -1 and +1 frameshifting.
Ribo-T ribosomes are severely impaired in +1 frameshiting. Efficiency dropped to 2% compared to 33% for WT. Replacing SD did not restore efficiency. WT frameshifting dropped when SD was replaced. SD-ASD interaction destabilizes the complex for +1 frameshifting.
Ribo-T uses SD sequences inefficiently for translation initiation. Luciferase induction increased four-fold with Ribo-T SD. Initiation occurred via internal loading, not re-initiation. Wild-type ribosomes cannot use Ribo-T SD sequences. Tethering modifies H44 orientation, affecting ASD recognition.
Ribo-T terminates translation less efficiently, increasing readthrough. Readthrough was 0.07% vs 0.013% for UAG. Readthrough was 0.26% vs 0.11% for UGA. Readthrough was 0.04% vs 0.01% for UAA. Ribo-T supports cell growth. Conformational dynamics are reduced in tethered ribosomes.
